syllabus.clause: the OpenAPI spec as the interop standard: config negotiation, load/commit with requirement assertions, multi-table transactions, views and register endpoints, credential vending and remote signing (X-Iceberg-Access-Delegation), server-side scan planning (featured in Iceberg 1.11), metrics reporting, SQL UDFs; the built-in OAuth2 token endpoint deprecated in favour of external identity providers.

at.step: Reveal: a real load, then a real race
Reveal: a real conflict, a real retry

sources.source: Apache Iceberg, REST Catalog OpenAPI Specification

items.item: All REST clients should first call the config route to get catalog configuration properties from the server to configure the catalog and its HTTP client
Defaults are applied before client configuration, and overrides are applied after defaults and client configuration
Requirements are assertions that will be validated before attempting to make and commit changes

at.step: Reveal: a real load, then a real race

items.item: The commitTransaction endpoint commits updates to multiple tables in an atomic operation
The register endpoint registers a table using a given metadata file location
The views endpoint returns all view identifiers under a namespace
A client signals via X-Iceberg-Access-Delegation which access mechanisms it supports, and the server may supply access via any or none of them
Clients must first check the storage-credentials field before checking config for vended credentials
Clients MUST use server-side scan planning via the planTableScan endpoint when the server requires it
SQL UDFs have a portable metadata format as part of the protocol
The oauth/tokens endpoint is marked deprecated for removal in the spec's own text
Apache Iceberg 1.11.0, which shipped server-side scan planning, was released on May 19, 2026
A real local REST catalog server implements a real subset of the actual OpenAPI spec -- config, load, commit-with-requirements -- over real HTTP, rather than simulating responses in-process.
The config negotiation demo asserts the real merge order (defaults, then client config, then overrides) rather than just printing values without checking the order matters.
The commit race names the exact requirement type (assert-current-snapshot-id) the spec itself defines, and the server checks it against its own real in-memory state under a lock.

at.step: Reveal: a real load, then a real race

items.item: The 409 response names the exact requirement that failed and the server's current state, demonstrated by a real error message, not a generic failure.

at.step: Reveal: a real conflict, a real retry

items.item: Credential vending is explicitly scoped out of the code (not just unmentioned) because issuing real down-scoped cloud credentials needs a real cloud STS-equivalent this sandbox cannot run.
Server-side scan planning is dated to a specific real Iceberg release (1.11.0, May 19, 2026) rather than described as a vague recent feature.
No deltalake/delta-rs/iceberg-python/pyiceberg library is used; both the server and the client are this script's own stdlib HTTP code, matching the chapter's from-scratch convention.
The scope boundary explicitly names what the script does not implement (most of the spec's endpoint surface, credential vending, a full reference server) rather than silently omitting it.
The predict step at step 2 and the predict step at step 5 are both answered correctly by the reveal steps that immediately follow them.

at.step: Predict: does a client just start sending requests?

items.item: The bridge/handoff framing correctly answers topic 31's handoff (the real, vendor-neutral protocol for the catalog this chapter already built) and hands off to topic 33's practical choice between format and catalog.
